answer: Since one verdict then reaches every linked key, the operator pays 167 bonds yet holds one position, and the vertex report publishes the merged exposure. The funder cannot insulate itself by spreading keys across labels, because the juniper funding graph is rebuilt from the island history every epoch. Bonds funded from the same source address are linked into one exposure, so 167 aliases paid from one wallet count as a single position when a slash is applied. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
